title: A leaking parcel is reported at the depot

plan.situation: Plover Arc Logistics' depot shift coordinator reports that parcel DL-023, on receiving lane L3, has an unknown leak: there is a wet patch under one carton and nobody has assessed the contents. Staff have stopped moving it and are keeping clear. The coordinator wants the carrier's safety lead to take over now, and does not want a driver or the customer involved. The desk has not sent any message yet.

facts.fact: DL-023 is on receiving lane L3 with a visible wet patch under one carton.
Staff have stopped moving the parcel and are keeping clear pending safety review.
Coordinator asks for the safety lead to take over now; do not route to a driver or ask the customer to collect.
The safety lead is not named in the record; the only recorded channel is the Depot work queue.

missing_information: What the parcel contains and whether it is hazardous (only the safety team can assess this)
The safety lead's name (not in the record)
Whether anyone has touched the liquid or been exposed to it
risk_flags: safety: an unknown substance is leaking at the depot
physical_handling: no one should move, open or clean up the parcel except qualified safety staff
No contents details or third-party information should be shared with anyone outside the safety process

authority_map.party: Plover Arc Logistics carrier safety lead/team
authority_map.controls: Hazard assessment, containment, handling, cleanup and release of DL-023

authority_map.party: Depot shift coordinator, Plover Arc Logistics
authority_map.controls: Keeping staff clear of lane L3 until safety staff arrive
Raising the incident and keeping the case coordinated; no handling decisions

wait_check.new_since_last_promise: The desk has made no earlier promise; event 001 reports a new safety incident and event 002 asks for escalation

plan.decision_summary: Escalate the DL-023 leak right away to Plover Arc Logistics' safety team through the Safety incident queue, and tell the depot coordinator it has been raised, without giving any handling advice.
plan.rationale: A leak of unknown contents is a safety hazard. Only qualified carrier safety staff can assess it, so it goes to the Safety incident queue as immediate, never to a driver or the customer. This is what the requester asked for.

actions.to_role: Carrier safety team, Plover Arc Logistics
actions.subject: URGENT safety incident: unknown leak, DL-023, receiving lane L3
actions.body:
Raised by Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk, at the request of the Plover Arc Logistics depot shift coordinator (09:10 UTC, 2026-02-24).

Shipment: DL-023. Location: receiving lane L3, depot.
Reported at 09:00 UTC: a wet patch is visible under one carton. Contents have not been assessed. Depot staff have stopped moving the parcel and are keeping clear pending safety review.

Please have a qualified safety lead take over this incident now: assess it, contain it, and decide on handling and cleanup. The depot has asked that it is not routed to a driver and that the customer is not asked to collect it. The desk has given no handling advice.

Please reply on this queue with an incident reference and confirm who is taking over.

actions.to_name: Depot shift coordinator, Plover Arc Logistics
actions.subject: DL-023 leak raised to your safety team
actions.body: At about 09:10 UTC we raised DL-023 (lane L3) as an urgent incident on the Safety incident queue for your safety lead to take over. We have not routed it to a driver or contacted the customer about collecting it. This tells you it has been raised; it is not yet confirmation that the safety lead has taken over. We will pass on the incident reference once safety confirms. Please keep following your site safety procedures until your safety team arrives, and tell us straight away if anything changes.

Check the Safety incident queue for an incident reference and confirmation that the safety lead has taken over DL-023. If there is none, escalate to the human supervisor queue to chase safety directly.
actions.purpose: Immediate follow-up under the safety queue rule

not_doing: Not giving any handling, cleanup, containment or 'it is safe' advice; that is the qualified safety team's decision
Not routing to a driver or asking the customer to collect, as the requester instructed
Not guessing or sharing what the parcel contains
Not confirming that the safety lead has taken over until there is an incident reference
Not inventing a name for the safety lead
plan.follow_up: At 09:25 UTC, check for a safety incident reference and confirmation that someone has taken over. If there is none, escalate right away to the human supervisor. Once the reference arrives, pass it to the depot coordinator and record it on the case.

review_rounds.plan_summary: Escalate the DL-023 leak right away to Plover Arc Logistics' safety team through the Safety incident queue, and tell the depot coordinator it has been raised, without giving any handling advice.

issues.problem: The lint tool flagged that the 'Safety incident queue' channel doesn't appear in the case record. The plan's own facts also say the only recorded channel is the Depot work queue. Still, this is the desk's standard internal route for safety escalations, not an unverified outside contact.
issues.fix: Confirm that the Safety incident queue is the desk's configured safety escalation route. If it isn't, send the escalation through the supervisor/safety route the desk has configured. Don't change the message content.

issues.problem: The action_class is 'request_operator_action', but the message is mainly a status update that the incident has been raised. It only reminds the depot to keep following its own site procedures, which it is already doing.
issues.fix: Optionally relabel the action as a status update. The content is fine and gives the depot new information: the incident has been raised and a reference is to follow.

review.summary: The plan sends the unknown leak straight to the carrier's qualified safety team as the requester asked. It gives no handling advice, doesn't claim the safety lead has taken over, keeps the driver and customer out of it, and sets a short follow-up that escalates to a human supervisor if safety doesn't confirm. The only issues are minor ones about the channel and labelling.
